metadata.title: Solvari Marketplace Stress Tests
metadata.description: Hypothetical business stressors used to shape the reference architecture, not claims of incidents at Solvari.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: Capture requests, distribute contacts, charge professionals, and report volume.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Retain confirmed intent, permissions, decision and agreement versions, recipients, commercial events, observable outcomes, and reversible corrections.
metadata.note: Integrated means represented in this source model, not implemented or tested in Solvari production. No probability or likelihood is assigned; no survival counts are invented.

stressors.name: Affiliate traffic produces duplicates and unwanted contact
stressors.detection: Rising duplicate rates, contact complaints, failed verification, and partner-origin quality outliers.
stressors.attractor: Acquisition targets encourage accepting more submissions while professionals pay for repeated or uncontactable requests.
stressors.businessReaction: Pause the affected source, preserve original references and sharing evidence, re-evaluate a bounded cohort, and reconcile credits and partner payables.
stressors.residue: Stable source identifiers, permission context, qualification versions, recipient history, and reversible corrections.

impacts.effect: Treat controlled useful contact as a condition of value.
Retain the original request lineage through rejection and settlement.
Separate duplication from legitimate repeated home projects.
Enforce idempotent partner references.
Reconcile only accepted payable demand.
Own source investigation and partner communication.
Benchmark relevant demand and professional trust rather than gross submissions.

stressors.name: A category demand spike outruns eligible regional supply
stressors.detection: More no-supply requests, aging capacity declarations, delayed useful contact, and rising campaign spend without response.
stressors.attractor: Marketing keeps attracting requests while unavailable firms receive unsuitable opportunities.
stressors.businessReaction: Expose honest no-match states, refresh declared capacity, constrain allocations, pause ineffective campaigns, and revise guidance for the affected category.
stressors.residue: Versioned region/category capacity, explicit pause state, no-match decisions, contact outcomes, and cohort launch gates.

impacts.effect: Protect acquisition value when supply and demand become imbalanced.
Return a clear no-match outcome instead of irrelevant contact.
Expire stale availability declarations.
Respect capacity changes and approved caps.
Explain local limitations before expanding a request.
Own supply readiness evidence.
Compare useful local responses, not only request volume.

stressors.name: Assistant guidance introduces a materially wrong project assumption
stressors.detection: Human-reviewed category samples show corrections, complaints, or sharp handoff deterioration after a configuration change.
stressors.attractor: A fluent explanation becomes a confirmed-looking brief and creates bad demand at scale.
stressors.businessReaction: Withdraw the affected guidance or assistant configuration, fall back to editable form intake, contact affected users where appropriate, and review the evidence before restoring it.
stressors.residue: Approved content versions, draft-versus-confirmed state, de-identified evaluation records, human release decisions, and fallback routing.

impacts.effect: Preserve informed choice and uncertainty in guidance.
Require the homeowner to confirm an editable brief.
Gate changes on category evaluation and support rollback.
Retain and withdraw source versions.
Keep a usable form path during assistant withdrawal.
Own release decisions and correction analysis.
Benchmark assistant adoption alongside correction quality.

stressors.name: Delivery retries or a package change double-charge professional demand
stressors.detection: Duplicate debit identifiers, unmatched reservations, invoice discrepancies, or campaign activity beyond the exit date.
stressors.attractor: Revenue records appear complete while the professional experiences unexplained spend.
stressors.businessReaction: Suspend affected billing paths, replay a bounded event set idempotently, append corrections, reconcile invoice and campaign state, and explain each affected account.
stressors.residue: Billable-event identity, immutable credit corrections, effective contract terms, reservation reconciliation, and notices.

impacts.effect: Make recurring participation conditional on explainable spend.
Reconcile costs before claiming retained value.
Enforce one logical debit per billable event.
Apply agreement changes at the correct effective time.
Show corrections and final balances together.
Own reconciliation and finance assurance.

stressors.name: A brand integration loses permissions or opening balances
stressors.detection: Duplicate professional identities, missing source IDs, unexplained balance differences, or mismatched permission versions in the pilot.
stressors.attractor: A migration is declared technically complete despite breaking commercial and data-use continuity.
stressors.businessReaction: Stop cutover expansion, reconcile the original records, restore disputed permissions or balances from authoritative history, and validate rollback before restarting.
stressors.residue: Source-to-target mappings, preserved effective agreements, purpose lineage, reconciled opening ledgers, and verified recovery checkpoints.

impacts.effect: Require operational and commercial readiness for each integration.
Use a bounded pilot and explicit go/no-go evidence.
Preserve reversible mappings rather than overwriting source identity.
Carry permission and authority history across brands.
Exercise recovery and verify restored state.
Own reconciliation evidence and cutover gates.
Expose unresolved migration exceptions to accountable operators.
